summary.text: Ed Case is the Democratic incumbent for Hawaii's 1st District, which he has represented since 2019 after earlier service in the Hawaii House and in Congress for the 2nd District (2002-2007). A Hilo native, he practiced law in Honolulu and was a senior executive at Outrigger before returning to Congress. He is running on his seniority and record in Congress, including his handling of COVID-19, Red Hill, and the Maui wildfires.

paragraphs.text: Case was born and raised in Hilo, Hawaii (born 1952, according to Ballotpedia), with family roots in Hawaii dating to 1896, according to his official biography. He graduated from Hawai'i Preparatory Academy in Kamuela.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Williams College (1975) and a law degree from the University of California College of the Law, San Francisco (formerly Hastings).

Before law school, he worked on Capitol Hill for three years as a legislative assistant to U.S. Rep. and later Sen. Spark Matsunaga. After law school he clerked for Hawaii Supreme Court Chief Justice William Richardson.

Case practiced law at Carlsmith Ball for about two decades, rising from associate to partner and managing partner, and then for seven years at Bays Lung Rose & Holma, where he was also managing attorney.

He served in the Hawaii House of Representatives from 1994 to 2002, representing Manoa and serving as Majority Leader, and then represented Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2002 to 2007.
Case later worked for five years as senior vice president and chief legal officer of Outrigger, a Hawaii hotel and resort company, before returning to Congress.

Case has represented Hawaii's 1st District since 2019 and serves on the House Appropriations Committee, including its Defense and Homeland Security subcommittees. He is co-founder and co-chair of the House Pacific Islands Caucus and vice chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus.
He won the August 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.0 percent of the vote. His official biography says he is married to Audrey (Nakamura) and that they have four children.
